title: Hades Fans Should Know About Amazon's Upcoming Sexy Greek God Animated Series
description: Hades and Hades 2 are beloved for many reasons--they're top-tier action roguelikes with incredible combat and smart progression systems that look and sound amazing--but one of the most enduring elements of both games is their storytelling. The writers at developer Supergiant Games have nailed the unique tone of the Greek pantheon and all its bitter rivalries, tragic loves and petty squabbles, and fans of the series might be looking for other works with similar vibes. Another popular exploration of Greek myth is Rachel Smythe's webcomic Lore Olympus, which focuses on, in the author's own words, "the friendships and the lies, the gossip and the wild parties, and of course, forbidden love" of the gods. And now, Variety is reporting that an animated version of Lore Olympus is on its way, courtesy of Amazon. The series will follow the plot of the comics, which reimagines the taking of Persephone, a key story within the lore of Hades, too. While the comic's versions of many of these characters look and act quite differently from the versions in Supergiants' games, fans of the games will definitely recognise certain story elements and character beats within the series' story. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Anthem Is Technically Still Playable, But You Probably Won't Be Able To
description: Last summer, EA announced that Anthem would be shut down in January 2026, and the game's final playable date passed earlier this month. But some fans aren't ready to let go of the former live-service shooter. And one player has demonstrated that Anthem can still be played on a private server. And799 posted a video on YouTube that showed off Anthem running after its shut-down date. And799 notes that this wasn't meant to be a revival project, and it was only intended for "my research and experiment." The video's description also states that it looks like "the majority of the player data [was] handled through BioWare's server instead of Blaze, and it is required for the game to be able to load offline." Theoretically, someone could continue the work started by And799 and get Anthem playable again. However, it's unlikely that EA would simply allow that to happen. Late last year, Concord fans revived the failed live-service shooter on their own, only to receive a take-down notice from Sony shortly thereafter. EA still retains ownership of Anthem and could have any revival of the game removed just as Sony did with Concord. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: New Hytale Update Adds Dinosaurs, New Sound Effects, Easier Storage Upgrades, And More
description: Hytale may have only launched into early access mere days ago, but its first update has already been rolled out, and it's quite the big one. Hypixel, after reacquiring its game from Riot, has been hard at work listening to player feedback and implementing changes. For its first update, Hytale now has dinosaurs populating its underground jungles. While the developer states that the prehistoric mobs are a "work in progress," they seem pretty solid early iterations. Hypixel says that these new NPCs required a "change to the environment in the biome," so if you're not finding any spawning near your base, try traveling to chunks farther away that you haven't explored just yet. As well as dinosaurs, some of the biomes have had minor adjustments. The Devastated Lands sewers have atmospheric effects and creatures will spawn. Areas beneath volcanoes will use volcanic environmental effects. Feran villages have had entity placements, textures, and interiors fixed. Finally, an invisible filler block behind the bench in the Forgotten Temple has been removed. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Has Officially Passed Elden Ring For The Most GOTY Titles Of All Time
description: After sweeping The Game Awards 2025 with a record-breaking number of both nominations and wins, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has edged out Elden Ring to become the most Game Of The Year-awarded title of all time. Expedition 33 has taken home a grand total of 436 GOTY titles, including major awards like The Game Awards GOTY as well as outlet-specific titles--including GameSpot's own Game of the Year--as tracked by users at Resetera. Elden Ring, which previously held the record for most GOTY awards, received a total of 429 titles. The GOTY stats show that Expedition 33 was last year's winner by a pretty long shot--the second most awarded game for 2025 was Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2, with only 38 Game of the Year titles. In 2022, by comparison, God Of War: Ragnarok put up a bit more of a fight against Elden Ring with a total of 118 GOTY wins. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Fallout Episode 6 Just Set The Stage For Some Game-Changing Confrontations
description: Last week’s episode saw us hit a boiling point between Lucy Maclean (Ella Purnell) and Cooper Howard (Walton Goggins)--one that resulted in him being power-fisted out a hotel window and impaled onto a pole below. Suffice to say, the stakes are getting high in season two of Fallout. Last we saw Lucy, she was knocked out and her father Hank (Kyle MacLachlan) was just arriving to pick her up. Meanwhile, Maximus (Aaron Moten) and Thaddeus’ (Johnny Pemberton) fates were left unknown in the aftermath of the chaos at Area 51. With the season reaching its most climatic point, let's break down the fallout (heh) of recent developments in this week’s episode. The episode opens up with a pre-war flashback showing Barbara Howard (Frances Turner) performing her day-to-day duties at Vault-Tec in preparation of the incoming apocalypse. Among these duties is choosing the blast radius size for the Los Angeles area and receiving an important piece of news: turns out, Vault-Tec’s waterchips have a 30% fail rate. She then takes a meeting with the fake Robert House (Rafi Silver) and Hank, during which House reveals his mind control device: the Automated Man. He promises Vault-Tec the piece of tech in exchange for the cold fusion relic and being able to experiment on vaults. Barbara inquires why he needs the cold fusion relic, but he informs her it's above her paygrade. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Fallout Episode 6 Just Introduced Super-Mutants (And Got An Iconic Movie Star To Play One)
description: From its vintage aesthetics and soundtrack to its captivating voice performances, Bethesda's Fallout series has unquestionably established itself as an iconic video game property. Now, with the television series from Prime, the post-apocalyptic adventure has firmly cemented itself as an iconic franchise, as week after week the series manages to capture all the elements that have delighted players throughout the years--especially the series' love of dishing out deep lore. Season two, episode six ups the ante on its deep cuts, offering plenty of lore and memorable moments of its own. Let’s break down some of the episode's easter eggs and biggest moments in this week’s episode of Fallout. Ron Perlman Ron PerlmanThis week’s episode saw Cooper Howard (Walton Goggins) saved from a bloody end by a massive Super-Mutant played by none other than beloved actor Ron Perlman. While Perlman is perhaps best known for his starring role in the original Hellboy movies, Fallout fans might recognize Perlman from another iconic performance. Back in 1997, it was Perlman who delivered the opening monologue heard in the original Fallout game (and then repeated throughout many other titles in the series). That's right--he’s the voice you hear saying “war… war never changes.” Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Fallout Episode 5's Easter Eggs Include A Throwback To The First Game’s Villain
description: This week’s venture into the Mojave Wasteland really hit home the idea that a lot of stories in the Fallout universe are intrinsically connected. From events that took place before the Great War, to events of the video games and the current timeline of the show, there’s no shortage of connections that form a deep and intricate web. With that in mind, let’s dive into some of the more notable points and easter eggs from episode five. A Fragmented Strip The Strip in Fallout: New VegasAs Lucy (Ella Purnell) and Cooper (Walton Goggins) explore The Strip and Freeside, the pair come to discover that the region is divided into sections by chainlink fences. These fences turn the strip from a massive throughstreet into smaller areas, akin to the level design from Fallout: New Vegas. While most may think this may have been an aesthetic choice, in actuality Obsidian Entertainment had to implement these fences because the game’s engine kept crashing when The Strip was a single large area. Talk about making the most of a bad situation. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Modder Combines PS5, Xbox Series X, And Switch 2 Into A Single Machine
description: Microsoft's "Everything is an Xbox" approach may have sent formerly Xbox-exclusive games to the PlayStation 5, but it's far from a two-way street. And it would take some kind of gaming miracle to get Nintendo to loan out its Switch franchises to other systems. But one gamer had the impossible dream of bringing an Xbox Series X, a PS5, and Switch 2 into a single machine, and she did it. The Ningtendo PXBOX 5 was created by 小宁子 XNZ, who shared the video above late last year (via GamesRadar). While the video is in Chinese, English subtitles are encoded for fans who want to follow the process. As XNZ explains in the video, she noticed that the consoles look very similar once they've been removed from their casings. The motherboards only take up a relatively small space, while the cooling system and power supply require a much larger area. XNZ's solution was to create a custom container inspired by the 2013 Mac Pro "trash can" design. Through trial and error, she came up with a three-sided internal design that allowed the motherboards to be situated on each side of the cooling system while sharing a single 250W PC power supply. Continue Reading at GameSpot
